habitat: Pairs occur in any broad-leaved woodland, thornveld or riverine bush, often with other birds of the same species and frequently in quite small trees.
summary: A common resident, identified by its small size, streaked breast, black malar streak and brown forehead. The male has a crimson crown and the female a black crown. The call is a high-pitched chittering ke-ke-ke-ke-ke-ke-kek. It taps quietly. Bill colour, eye, legs, wings and the tail colour were not described. The Kemp paper name Cardinal Woodpecker and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Golden-tailed Woodpecker is larger. The male’s whole crown is red with black spots and he has a red malar streak. Cardinal Woodpecker has a brown forehead.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman says the male crown is crimson. That colour is not in the vocabulary, so the crown is stored as red and the word crimson stays in the pattern. The immature was not described. Bill colour, eye, legs, wings and tail colour were not given. The female side photograph is crossed by branches. No flight photograph was found. The grade A call is from Kruger near Skukuza. Its catalogue filename already includes a 600 Hz high-pass, so no further filter is claimed. Population figures, the Kemp paper name Cardinal Woodpecker and the code RB were left unchanged.
